title: $11B midterm ad race may drive record CPMs in key battlegrounds

facts.fact: An eMarketer article published June 18, 2026 is headlined that the $11B midterm ad race may drive record CPMs in key battlegrounds.
facts.quote: $11B midterm ad race may drive record CPMs in key battlegrounds

facts.fact: EMARKETER forecasts that political ad spending for the 2026 midterms will reach $11.07 billion across all media channels.
facts.quote: Political ad spending for the 2026 midterms is projected to reach $11.07 billion across all media channels

facts.fact: EMARKETER projects 2026 midterm political ad spending to be 21.4% higher than the last midterm cycle.
facts.quote: This represents a 21.4% increase over the last midterm cycle

facts.fact: EMARKETER's 2026 midterm political ad forecast of $11.07 billion nearly matches the $11.65 billion spent during the 2024 presidential election.
EMARKETER projects traditional broadcast television to secure the largest share of 2026 political ad spending at $5.60 billion.
facts.quote: traditional broadcast television still secures the largest share of spending at $5.60 billion

facts.fact: EMARKETER projects total digital political ad spending to reach $3.84 billion in 2026.
facts.quote: Total digital political spend is projected to reach

facts.fact: EMARKETER projects connected TV (CTV) political ad spending to reach $2.70 billion in 2026.
facts.quote: driven by connected TV (CTV), which is climbing to

facts.fact: EMARKETER projects CTV political ad spending to show a 194% increase over 2022.
The article names California, Ohio, and Texas as high-stakes battleground states whose programmatic inventory will be affected by political spending.
facts.quote: particularly for brands targeting high-stakes battleground states like California, Ohio, and Texas

facts.fact: Senate races are expected to pull in $2.8 billion in 2026 midterm ad spend, per AdImpact projections.
facts.quote: Senate races alone are expected to pull in $2.8 billion, while highly competitive House races are on track to absorb $2.2 billion

facts.fact: Highly competitive House races are on track to absorb $2.2 billion in 2026 midterm ad spend, per AdImpact projections.
facts.quote: highly competitive House races are on track to absorb $2.2 billion—a staggering 40% increase over 2022 levels

facts.fact: State legislative, gubernatorial, and down-ballot contests are expected to account for roughly $3.9 billion of midterm ad spend, per AdImpact.
facts.quote: State legislative, gubernatorial, and down ballot contests will account for more than a third of all historical midterm ad spend, totaling roughly $3.9 billion

facts.fact: Michigan is projected to absorb over $1 billion in total political advertising in the 2026 cycle, per Kinetiq Political Insights.
facts.quote: Michigan is projected to absorb over $1 billion in total political advertising this cycle

facts.fact: The Atlanta area is estimated to be the most expensive media market for the 2026 midterms, commanding an estimated $591 million.
facts.quote: the Atlanta area is tracking to be the most expensive media market, commanding an estimated $591 million

facts.fact: Streaming video is expected to cross a 25% threshold of total political ad spend in 2026.
facts.quote: where streaming video will cross an unprecedented 25% threshold of total political spend
